1018903.title: Street canopy on the sunlit sidewalk
1018903.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–3 of 13 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 3 of those 3 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. 1015174.title: External wall insulation / added facade admittance
1015174.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 50.5 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.3 K absorbed shortwave and 1.7 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (43% solar, 57% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.1 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1.7 K of the 2.9 K of positive driver is longwave arriving from the buildings opposite (57%), against 1.3 K of sun. Shading this wall would treat the smaller term: the lever is the fabric's own admittance, which governs how much of that net radiation it absorbs rather than sheds. 1017127.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–4 of 20 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 4 of those 4 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 20 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1017221.title: External wall insulation / added facade admittance
1017221.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 46.2 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.2 K absorbed shortwave and 1.6 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (43% solar, 57% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.1 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1.6 K of the 2.9 K of positive driver is longwave arriving from the buildings opposite (57%), against 1.2 K of sun. Shading this wall would treat the smaller term: the lever is the fabric's own admittance, which governs how much of that net radiation it absorbs rather than sheds. Night purge ventilation is excluded here, explicitly. The sky term is only -0.1 K and the night recovery reads "limited": this surface cannot radiate to the sky, so there is no cool night air to purge with and the measure would move warm air through the building for a whole night and spend fan energy doing it.

Energy is the opaque conduction term re-evaluated with the new build-up's U-value, not scaled from the facade temperature delta — which for this measure points the WRONG WAY: insulation lowers the wall's admittance, so its outer face sheds less into its own mass and runs +0.51 K, and scaling by that read a fabric improvement as a cooling penalty. Both effects are carried here, and the U-value dominates. The heating-season saving is the fabric calculation against this building's own 39,296-67,438 heating degree hours, counted from its hourly air series against a 12-18 °C balance point rather than a published normal. It covers the SPANDREL only: exterior insulation stops at the sight line, so the glass keeps its U-value and its losses, which is why this measure is prescribed on masonry. The carbon of the heat it saves is not netted — no fuel-combustion coefficient is in the constants table.

1019141.winter_cost: Canopy lowers the sky view factor slightly, which slows night-time radiative cooling year-round; deciduous species return most of the winter beam. The daytime summer gain dominates decisively and the model reproduces both signs.
1019141.does_not_fix: It does not reach 4–13 of 1–13. Those are covered by floors 4–13 by external operable shading (louvres or retractable awning). Its reach is bands 0–1 and no further, which is a statement about the measure and not about this building. It does nothing for the roof.

1016894.title: Street canopy on the sunlit sidewalk
1016894.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–3 of 13 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 3 of those 3 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 13 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.
why_parts: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–3 of 13 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 3 of those 3 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk.

This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 13 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.
1016894.winter_cost: Canopy lowers the sky view factor slightly, which slows night-time radiative cooling year-round; deciduous species return most of the winter beam. The daytime summer gain dominates decisively and the model reproduces both signs.
1016894.does_not_fix: It does not reach 4–13 of 1–13. Nothing in this schedule reaches floors 4–13. Its reach is bands 0–1 and no further, which is a statement about the measure and not about this building. It does nothing for the roof.

effect.source: re-solved

1016894.effect_note: ['The canyon solution is one-dimensional across the street: it resolves height and orientation but not along-street variation, and there is no advective coupling between adjacent canyons. Treating several blocks returns several independent solutions, so the AIR temperature delta is an under-estimate at scale while the surface and radiant deltas are roughly right.', "Deltas are instantaneous at the hours solved, not daily means. Use window='day' for a diurnal picture.", 'Tree cover is a canopy FRACTION, not a species or a planting plan, and it assumes an established canopy — not the first ten years of one.'] Energy and person-hours are a first-order linear scaling of this building's own load by the re-solved facade delta over the driving temperature difference, not a second re-solve; the facade kelvin figure is the model's own answer and the rest is interpretation. The winter heating penalty is inferred from the re-solved winter facade delta at half the summer coefficient; it is the least certain figure on this prescription. Not priced against this building: a street tree is a Parks Department planting on public right-of-way, not a charge against this building. The measure is still selected and its effect is still re-solved; what is absent is a capex line, not a benefit.

1015898.title: Fixed horizontal overhang
1015898.why: Floor 2 sits in band 1 and peaks at 52.9 °C. The attribution splits that as 2.2 K absorbed shortwave and 1.2 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (64% solar, 36% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.4 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". The north-west, north-west, south-west and south-west faces carry the load. At the peak hour (18:00 EDT) the sun is 26° above the horizon and 70° off the wall normal, a profile angle of 55°. P = 2.10 m · cos(70°) / tan(26°) = 1.46 m.
why_parts: Floor 2 sits in band 1 and peaks at 52.9 °C. The attribution splits that as 2.2 K absorbed shortwave and 1.2 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (64% solar, 36% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.4 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited".
The north-west, north-west, south-west and south-west faces carry the load. At the peak hour (18:00 EDT) the sun is 26° above the horizon and 70° off the wall normal, a profile angle of 55°.
1015898.winter_cost: An overhang sized on the summer profile angle passes most of the winter beam underneath it, because the winter sun is lower. This is the one shading device whose seasonal penalty is small by construction, and it is why it is preferred wherever the geometry allows it.
programme: Landmarks Preservation Commission review if applicable
1015898.does_not_fix: It does not reach 1 and 4–10 of 1–10. Those are covered by floors 1 by external operable shading (louvres or retractable awning); floors 4–10 by external operable shading (louvres or retractable awning). On the treated storeys it leaves the north-east, south-east elevations at full load. It does nothing for the roof.

Person-hours are the same lever carried through to exposure: 0.23 K off the free-running indoor mean on the worst treated storey, converted to hours by the density of this building's own annual air series at the 28 °C threshold, so a floor already far above it is credited with little and a floor sitting on it with a great deal. Linearised about the current offset and silent on the daily swing, which the admittance procedure damps and this does not differentiate.

geometry.infeasible_reason: No fixed device works on this wall. At its peak hour the sun is only 26° above the horizon and just 20° off the wall normal — low and nearly square-on at the same time. 1080449.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–2 of 10 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 2 of those 2 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 10 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1017084.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 53.0 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.3 K absorbed shortwave and 1.5 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (46% solar, 54% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.1 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1.5 K of the 2.9 K of positive driver is longwave arriving from the buildings opposite (54%), against 1.3 K of sun. 1018885.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–4 of 18 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 4 of those 4 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 18 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1088911.title: External wall insulation / added facade admittance
1088911.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 43.8 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.2 K absorbed shortwave and 1.3 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (46% solar, 54% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.3 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1.3 K of the 2.5 K of positive driver is longwave arriving from the buildings opposite (54%), against 1.2 K of sun. Shading this wall would treat the smaller term: the lever is the fabric's own admittance, which governs how much of that net radiation it absorbs rather than sheds. Night purge ventilation is excluded here, explicitly. The sky term is only -0.3 K and the night recovery reads "limited": this surface cannot radiate to the sky, so there is no cool night air to purge with and the measure would move warm air through the building for a whole night and spend fan energy doing it.

That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1078763.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 47.2 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.3 K absorbed shortwave and 1.6 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (45% solar, 55% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.1 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1.6 K of the 2.9 K of positive driver is longwave arriving from the buildings opposite (55%), against 1.3 K of sun. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 62 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1018463.title: Street canopy on the sunlit sidewalk
1018463.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–3 of 12 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 3 of those 3 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. 1019107.title: External wall insulation / added facade admittance
1019107.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 52.0 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.5 K absorbed shortwave and 1.5 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (49% solar, 51% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.1 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1.5 K of the 3.0 K of positive driver is longwave arriving from the buildings opposite (51%), against 1.5 K of sun. Shading this wall would treat the smaller term: the lever is the fabric's own admittance, which governs how much of that net radiation it absorbs rather than sheds. 1078761.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 48.8 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.2 K absorbed shortwave and 1.5 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (44% solar, 56% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.1 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1016990.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 46.6 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.3 K absorbed shortwave and 1.5 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (45% solar, 55% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.2 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1.5 K of the 2.8 K of positive driver is longwave arriving from the buildings opposite (55%), against 1.3 K of sun. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 15 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1038647.title: External wall insulation / added facade admittance
1038647.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 43.6 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.1 K absorbed shortwave and 1.3 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (44% solar, 56% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.2 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1.3 K of the 2.4 K of positive driver is longwave arriving from the buildings opposite (56%), against 1.1 K of sun. Shading this wall would treat the smaller term: the lever is the fabric's own admittance, which governs how much of that net radiation it absorbs rather than sheds. Night purge ventilation is excluded here, explicitly. The sky term is only -0.2 K and the night recovery reads "limited": this surface cannot radiate to the sky, so there is no cool night air to purge with and the measure would move warm air through the building for a whole night and spend fan energy doing it.

The heating-season saving is the fabric calculation against this building's own 39,296-67,438 heating degree hours, counted from its hourly air series against a 12-18 °C balance point rather than a published normal. It covers the SPANDREL only: exterior insulation stops at the sight line, so the glass keeps its U-value and its losses, which is why this measure is prescribed on masonry. The carbon of the heat it saves is not netted — no fuel-combustion coefficient is in the constants table.

1038655.title: External wall insulation / added facade admittance
1038655.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 50.7 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.1 K absorbed shortwave and 1.2 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (48% solar, 52% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.3 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1.2 K of the 2.3 K of positive driver is longwave arriving from the buildings opposite (52%), against 1.1 K of sun. Shading this wall would treat the smaller term: the lever is the fabric's own admittance, which governs how much of that net radiation it absorbs rather than sheds. Night purge ventilation is excluded here, explicitly. 1019089.title: External operable shading (louvres or retractable awning)
1019089.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 53.2 °C. The attribution splits that as 2.2 K absorbed shortwave and 1.4 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (62% solar, 38% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.2 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". The north-west, south-east and south-west faces carry the load. At the peak hour (15:00 EDT) the sun is 59° above the horizon and 35° off the wall normal, a profile angle of 64°. P = 2.10 m · cos(35°) / tan(59°) = 1.02 m. 43% of this face's annual sun arrives in the heating season, above the 35% at which a fixed device costs more in January than it saves in July. The fixed horizontal overhang the geometry selected is replaced by an operable one that retracts.

effect.source: re-solved facade delta; energy from the solar lever

1020201.effect_note: ['The canyon solution is one-dimensional across the street: it resolves height and orientation but not along-street variation, and there is no advective coupling between adjacent canyons. Use window='day' for a diurnal picture.", 'Tree cover is a canopy FRACTION, not a species or a planting plan, and it assumes an established canopy — not the first ten years of one.'] Energy and person-hours are a first-order linear scaling of this building's own load by the re-solved facade delta over the driving temperature difference, not a second re-solve; the facade kelvin figure is the model's own answer and the rest is interpretation. The winter heating penalty is inferred from the re-solved winter facade delta at half the summer coefficient; it is the least certain figure on this prescription. Energy is not scaled from the facade temperature delta alone for this measure. It is the cooling-season expression in loads.py re-evaluated against this device's own shading fraction on the transmitted beam, and the re-solved facade delta on the conducted skin load. Both terms are real for a device fitted outside the glass and they are different halves of the same sum, so neither is double-counted. The peak figure is taken at the hour the WHOLE BUILDING peaks, not at each face's own worst hour, because a demand charge is billed on the one highest reading the meter takes and a west elevation's evening maximum is not when a building that peaks mid-afternoon gets metered. It takes no heating-season penalty: this device retracts, so the winter beam is still available. Person-hours are the same lever carried through to exposure: 0.27 K off the free-running indoor mean on the worst treated storey, converted to hours by the density of this building's own annual air series at the 28 °C threshold, so a floor already far above it is credited with little and a floor sitting on it with a great deal. Linearised about the current offset and silent on the daily swing, which the admittance procedure damps and this does not differentiate.

1020201.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 46.2 °C. 1021913.title: Street canopy on the sunlit sidewalk
1021913.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–2 of 6 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 2 of those 2 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 6 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.
why_parts: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–2 of 6 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 2 of those 2 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk.

1020180.title: Street canopy on the sunlit sidewalk
1020180.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–2 of 10 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 2 of those 2 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 10 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1017179.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–2 of 8 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 2 of those 2 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 8 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1018905.title: Street canopy on the sunlit sidewalk
1018905.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–2 of 8 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 2 of those 2 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 8 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1019150.title: External wall insulation / added facade admittance
1019150.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 45.5 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.3 K absorbed shortwave and 1.7 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (43% solar, 57% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.1 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1.7 K of the 2.9 K of positive driver is longwave arriving from the buildings opposite (57%), against 1.3 K of sun. Shading this wall would treat the smaller term: the lever is the fabric's own admittance, which governs how much of that net radiation it absorbs rather than sheds. Night purge ventilation is excluded here, explicitly. The sky term is only -0.1 K and the night recovery reads "limited": this surface cannot radiate to the sky, so there is no cool night air to purge with and the measure would move warm air through the building for a whole night and spend fan energy doing it.

Both effects are carried here, and the U-value dominates. The heating-season saving is the fabric calculation against this building's own 39,296-67,438 heating degree hours, counted from its hourly air series against a 12-18 °C balance point rather than a published normal. It covers the SPANDREL only: exterior insulation stops at the sight line, so the glass keeps its U-value and its losses, which is why this measure is prescribed on masonry. The carbon of the heat it saves is not netted — no fuel-combustion coefficient is in the constants table.

1020361.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 49.0 °C. 1038646.title: Street canopy on the sunlit sidewalk
1038646.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–3 of 14 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 3 of those 3 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 14 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

Both failures have one cause and no larger dimension fixes either. The devices that work here are operable — retracted outside the two or three hours that matter — or a glazing unit with a solar heat gain coefficient at or below 0.25.

Person-hours are the same lever carried through to exposure: 0.36 K off the free-running indoor mean on the worst treated storey, converted to hours by the density of this building's own annual air series at the 28 °C threshold, so a floor already far above it is credited with little and a floor sitting on it with a great deal. 1078801.title: Street canopy on the sunlit sidewalk
1078801.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floor 1 of 5 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 1 of those 1 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 5 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.
why_parts: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floor 1 of 5 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 1 of those 1 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk.

1078801.winter_cost: Canopy lowers the sky view factor slightly, which slows night-time radiative cooling year-round; deciduous species return most of the winter beam. The daytime summer gain dominates decisively and the model reproduces both signs.
1078801.does_not_fix: It does not reach 2–5 of 1–5. Those are covered by floors 2–5 by external operable shading (louvres or retractable awning). Its reach is bands 0–1 and no further, which is a statement about the measure and not about this building. It does nothing for the roof.

1024813.title: External wall insulation / added facade admittance
1024813.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 47.2 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.2 K absorbed shortwave and 1.5 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (45% solar, 55% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.1 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1.5 K of the 2.8 K of positive driver is longwave arriving from the buildings opposite (55%), against 1.2 K of sun. Shading this wall would treat the smaller term: the lever is the fabric's own admittance, which governs how much of that net radiation it absorbs rather than sheds. Night purge ventilation is excluded here, explicitly. The sky term is only -0.1 K and the night recovery reads "limited": this surface cannot radiate to the sky, so there is no cool night air to purge with and the measure would move warm air through the building for a whole night and spend fan energy doing it.

The carbon of the heat it saves is not netted — no fuel-combustion coefficient is in the constants table.

That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1018953.title: Street canopy on the sunlit sidewalk
1018953.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–5 of 24 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 5 of those 5 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1018902.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 52.3 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.5 K absorbed shortwave and 1.4 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (51% solar, 49% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.2 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1018902.title: Street canopy on the sunlit sidewalk
1018902.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–3 of 12 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 3 of those 3 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 12 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1020212.title: Street canopy on the sunlit sidewalk
1020212.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–2 of 6 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 2 of those 2 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 6 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.
why_parts: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–2 of 6 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 2 of those 2 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk.

1020212.winter_cost: Canopy lowers the sky view factor slightly, which slows night-time radiative cooling year-round; deciduous species return most of the winter beam. The daytime summer gain dominates decisively and the model reproduces both signs.

1017204.title: Street canopy on the sunlit sidewalk
1017204.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floor 1 of 4 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 1 of those 1 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 4 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1038652.title: External wall insulation / added facade admittance
1038652.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 51.9 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.1 K absorbed shortwave and 1.3 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (47% solar, 53% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.4 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1.3 K of the 2.4 K of positive driver is longwave arriving from the buildings opposite (53%), against 1.1 K of sun. Shading this wall would treat the smaller term: the lever is the fabric's own admittance, which governs how much of that net radiation it absorbs rather than sheds. Night purge ventilation is excluded here, explicitly. The sky term is only -0.4 K and the night recovery reads "limited": this surface cannot radiate to the sky, so there is no cool night air to purge with and the measure would move warm air through the building for a whole night and spend fan energy doing it.

Both effects are carried here, and the U-value dominates. The heating-season saving is the fabric calculation against this building's own 39,296-67,438 heating degree hours, counted from its hourly air series against a 12-18 °C balance point rather than a published normal. It covers the SPANDREL only: exterior insulation stops at the sight line, so the glass keeps its U-value and its losses, which is why this measure is prescribed on masonry. The carbon of the heat it saves is not netted — no fuel-combustion coefficient is in the constants table.

1017214.title: Street canopy on the sunlit sidewalk
1017214.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floor 1 of 4 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 1 of those 1 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 4 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1018923.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 42.4 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.2 K absorbed shortwave and 1.3 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (48% solar, 52% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.3 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1.3 K of the 2.5 K of positive driver is longwave arriving from the buildings opposite (52%), against 1.2 K of sun. Shading this wall would treat the smaller term: the lever is the fabric's own admittance, which governs how much of that net radiation it absorbs rather than sheds. Night purge ventilation is excluded here, explicitly. The sky term is only -0.3 K and the night recovery reads "limited": this surface cannot radiate to the sky, so there is no cool night air to purge with and the measure would move warm air through the building for a whole night and spend fan energy doing it.

A horizontal overhang would have to project 4.08 m against a 1.5 m cutoff, because tan(altitude) is in the denominator and the altitude is small; vertical fins would need a depth-to-spacing ratio of 2.7:1 against a limit of 1.0, because the beam is normal in plan and there is nothing for a fin to intercept. Both failures have one cause and no larger dimension fixes either. The devices that work here are operable — retracted outside the two or three hours that matter — or a glazing unit with a solar heat gain coefficient at or below 0.25.

1025184.title: Street canopy on the sunlit sidewalk
1025184.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floor 1 of 5 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 1 of those 1 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 5 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 3 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1014260.why: Floor 1 sits in band 0 and peaks at 50.8 °C. The attribution splits that as 1.7 K absorbed shortwave and 1.2 K longwave trapped from the surfaces opposite (59% solar, 41% trapping of the positive drivers), against -0.4 K of relief to the sky — night recovery "limited". 1014260.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–3 of 14 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 3 of those 3 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 14 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.

1017218.title: External operable shading (louvres or retractable awning)

geometry.infeasible_reason: No fixed device works on this wall. At its peak hour the sun is only 26° above the horizon and just 20° off the wall normal — low and nearly square-on at the same time. A horizontal overhang would have to project 4.09 m against a 1.5 m cutoff, because tan(altitude) is in the denominator and the altitude is small; vertical fins would need a depth-to-spacing ratio of 2.8:1 against a limit of 1.0, because the beam is normal in plan and there is nothing for a fin to intercept. 1020333.title: Street canopy on the sunlit sidewalk
1020333.why: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–3 of 14 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 3 of those 3 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk. This measure reaches band 1 and no further: a mature London plane in Midtown is 12 to 15 m to the crown against a building of 14 storeys, so it does nothing whatever for the floors above it. That is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a measure list that happens not to mention it.
why_parts: Bands 0–1 of the ten solved bands — floors 1–3 of 14 — sit within reach of a street canopy, and 3 of those 3 storeys are solar-dominant at the sidewalk.

1020333.winter_cost: Canopy lowers the sky view factor slightly, which slows night-time radiative cooling year-round; deciduous species return most of the winter beam. The daytime summer gain dominates decisively and the model reproduces both signs.
1020333.does_not_fix: It does not reach 4–14 of 1–14. Those are covered by floors 4–14 by external operable shading (louvres or retractable awning). Its reach is bands 0–1 and no further, which is a statement about the measure and not about this building. It does nothing for the roof.
